source.orchestrator: route-thinking-mode is the coordinator control plane, not a peer evaluator
source.purpose: Independent single-mode evaluations of one frozen task packet

modes.name: Abductive reasoning
modes.procedure: List plausible explanations; rank them by explanatory fit and test cost; state what evidence each predicts; choose the safest discriminating test; update confidence from results.
modes.expected: Ranked hypotheses, supporting and contradicting evidence, next discriminating test.

modes.name: Abstract thinking
modes.procedure: Separate essential behaviour from incidental details. Define concepts, interfaces, contracts, invariants, ownership boundaries and assumptions. Avoid abstractions without a demonstrated benefit.
modes.expected: Minimal conceptual model, contracts and invariants, open decisions, implementation implications.

modes.name: Adversarial thinking
modes.procedure: Assume malformed inputs, hostile instructions, unexpected sequences and partial failures. Identify attack and misuse paths; test safely within authority; prioritise mitigations.
modes.expected: Prioritised attack/failure scenarios, evidence, mitigations.

modes.name: Analytical thinking
modes.procedure: Break the issue into testable parts. Establish a baseline; inspect the smallest relevant evidence; isolate variables; compare expected and actual behaviour; choose a discriminating test.
modes.expected: Failing boundary, evidence, leading cause or ranked hypotheses, decisive test and result.

modes.name: Causal thinking
modes.procedure: Separate correlation from causation. Map event sequence and mechanisms; identify confounders; use controlled comparisons or interventions; test whether the cause predicts outcomes.
modes.expected: Causal hypothesis, evidence, alternatives, confirmation test.

modes.name: Computational thinking
modes.procedure: Define inputs, outputs, invariants, constraints and edge cases. Decompose data and control flow; make ambiguous rules explicit; express the smallest testable algorithm.
modes.expected: Executable logic or concrete implementation, assumptions, edge cases and correctness tests.

modes.name: Concrete thinking
modes.procedure: Use exact artefacts, paths, versions, logs, API contracts, settings and observed values. Reproduce a concrete example; separate observations from interpretation.
modes.expected: Fact-based account with exact observations and reproducible test.

modes.name: Convergent thinking
modes.procedure: Set decision criteria; compare options consistently; eliminate infeasible choices; weigh benefit, cost, risk, reversibility and maintenance; explain why the winner beats alternatives.
modes.expected: Recommendation, comparison, rationale, conditions that would change the decision.

modes.name: Critical thinking
modes.procedure: Separate facts, inference, assumptions and unknowns. Check source authority and freshness; seek contradictions and counterexamples; compare options against actual success criteria and risk.
modes.expected: Strongest supported conclusion, alternatives, confidence, unknowns, smallest decision-changing check.

modes.name: Decomposition thinking
modes.procedure: Break the outcome into coherent work units ordered by dependency and risk. Identify critical path, parallel work, blockers, approval boundaries and acceptance checks.
modes.expected: Ordered tasks, dependencies, first useful increment and completion criteria.

modes.name: Deductive reasoning
modes.procedure: State governing rules; apply them to the concrete case; derive expected outputs; check boundary conditions; compare implementation or results against the derived expectation.
modes.expected: Rule-to-conclusion chain and testable expected results.

modes.name: Design thinking
modes.procedure: Identify user, job-to-be-done, current workaround, pain point and desired outcome. Separate needs from proposed features; test the riskiest assumption cheaply; define observable success.
modes.expected: Problem statement, user and constraints, testable requirements, key assumption and validation.

modes.name: Divergent thinking
modes.procedure: Generate meaningfully different approaches by varying assumptions and solution classes. Include simple, unconventional and low-cost options; defer selection; note risks.
modes.expected: Diverse shortlist with distinguishing ideas and main risks.

modes.name: Failure-mode thinking
modes.procedure: Identify plausible failure modes, causes, effects, detection signals, blast radius and recovery. Prioritise by severity and likelihood; specify prevention, fallback, rollback and recovery tests.
modes.expected: Highest-priority failure modes, mitigations, recovery proof and unresolved risk.

modes.name: Feedback-loop thinking
modes.procedure: Define outcome and baseline metric. Inspect existing telemetry; find repeated friction, failure clusters, delays or regressions; choose one bounded improvement and compare results.
modes.expected: Evidence, leverage point, bounded experiment, success metric and follow-up trigger.

modes.name: First-principles thinking
modes.procedure: State outcome and hard constraints. Separate facts from assumptions and convention; reduce to necessary truths; rebuild candidate solutions from fundamentals; test feasibility.
modes.expected: Fundamental requirements, challenged assumptions and simplest viable solution.

modes.name: Inductive reasoning
modes.procedure: Collect multiple observations; identify stable trends; check sample size, bias and exceptions; form a qualified generalisation; seek counterexamples.
modes.expected: Qualified pattern or hypothesis, evidence base and falsification condition.

modes.name: Interaction modelling
modes.procedure: Trace user from entry point to goal, including actions, system responses, feedback, errors, recovery and exits. Identify ambiguous states and unnecessary steps.
modes.expected: Step-by-step journey, friction points, failure paths and acceptance criteria.

modes.name: Iterative thinking
modes.procedure: Define acceptance first; inspect baseline; build the smallest complete increment; test it; fix regressions; expand only when evidence requires it; preserve reversibility.
modes.expected: Working increment, test evidence, remaining gap and next iteration.

modes.name: Lateral thinking
modes.procedure: Restate the goal without the current proposed solution. Challenge preferences mistaken for necessities; explore alternative mechanisms; check legality, security and hidden costs.
modes.expected: Unconventional alternatives with feasibility checks.

modes.name: Linear thinking
modes.procedure: Order deterministic steps by prerequisites. Define expected result and stop condition at each step; execute one at a time; inspect outputs; stop and reassess on surprises.
modes.expected: Sequential procedure, checkpoints, stop conditions and recovery guidance.

modes.name: Pattern recognition thinking
modes.procedure: Compare current evidence with prior instances; identify similarities and differences; test whether the candidate pattern predicts outcomes; avoid assuming resemblance proves shared cause.
modes.expected: Candidate pattern, matching evidence, exceptions and validation.

modes.name: Probabilistic thinking
modes.procedure: Estimate relative likelihoods without false precision; consider impact; update estimates as evidence arrives; prioritise checks by information gain and risk reduction.
modes.expected: Ranked possibilities, uncertainty and highest-value next check.

modes.name: Silo thinking
modes.procedure: Define one component boundary and explicitly exclude unrelated context. Test the isolated component, then reintegrate and verify cross-component contracts.
modes.expected: Isolated result and integration checks.

modes.name: State-machine thinking
modes.procedure: Enumerate valid states; define events and allowed transitions; specify guards, side effects, timeouts, retries, terminal and invalid transitions; test transition coverage.
modes.expected: State/transition model and normal, failure, retry and terminal tests.

modes.name: Systems thinking
modes.procedure: Map system boundary, users, components, dependencies, data/control flows, feedback loops and second-order effects. Identify a leverage point that improves the whole outcome.
modes.expected: Compact system map, leverage point, trade-offs and next evidence-backed action.

modes.name: Trade-off thinking
modes.procedure: Identify competing goals and non-negotiable constraints. Compare options across relevant cost, speed, reliability, security, performance and complexity; expose sacrifices.
modes.expected: Decision comparison and chosen compromise.

modes.name: User-journey thinking
modes.procedure: Follow the real user entry point through interfaces, permissions, handoffs, processing, persistence and confirmation. Include failure and recovery; do not equate a click or HTTP success with completion.
modes.expected: End-to-end test, observed checkpoints, final user-visible state and broken handoffs.
